Classification guard: the authored edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, mechanismCategory INFECTIOUS_SPREAD). The located evidence is referral and surgical-case-series level - infectious keratitis eyes with graded corneal opacity and higher-order aberrations that correlate with visual acuity, and keratoplasty series performed for herpetic corneal scarring - so individual claims require organism and depth characterization with dates, slit-lamp and topographic documentation of the opacity, chronology, and exclusion of the competing causes listed on the edge.

Prior-closure guard: the master-resolution program closed the harvested keratitis-to-visual-impairment proposition (PMID 37802392) as FINAL-CLOSE-PROPOSITION-MISMATCH with no approved targets, and that proposition is NOT reasserted here - no visual-impairment, blindness, or night-blindness edge is authored. The authored target is the structural corneal-sequela identity (corneal-scarring), and the proposition is limited to the opacity itself rather than to functional loss.

Duplicate-scope guard: the corneal-scarring identity already receives the adenoviral-epidemic-keratoconjunctivitis subepithelial-infiltrate window from conjunctivitis and the cicatricial-autoimmune window from cicatricial pemphigoid; this batch adds the microbial and herpetic stromal route on keratitis-primary evidence (bacterial, fungal, Acanthamoeba, and herpes simplex) rather than restating the adenoviral infiltrate pathway, and no glaucoma, cataract, uveitis, or dry-eye edge is authored because those windows belong to their own primaries.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 50 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - keratitis to corneal-scarring (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true; mechanismCategory INFECTIOUS_SPREAD. The proposition rests on the Shimizu 2017 retrospective consecutive series of 63 eyes of 62 patients with corneal scarring due to Acanthamoeba keratitis (20 eyes), bacterial keratitis (35 eyes), and fungal keratitis (8 eyes) compared with 18 normal subjects, in which total-cornea higher-order aberrations within a 4-mm diameter were significantly larger in the keratitis eyes (Acanthamoeba 1.15 +/- 2.06 micrometre, bacterial 0.91 +/- 0.88, fungal 1.39 +/- 1.46) than in controls (0.09 +/- 0.01; all P < .001), an asymmetric topographic pattern was the commonest (30%, 51.4%, and 37.5% respectively), and visual acuity correlated significantly with anterior-surface (R = 0.764), posterior-surface (R = 0.745), and total-cornea (R = 0.669) aberrations (all P < .0001); it rests also on the Altay 2017 retrospective analysis of 55 eyes undergoing penetrating keratoplasty for corneal scarring caused by herpes simplex keratitis, in which 42 eyes had a quiescent herpetic scar and 13 had developed a descemetocele or perforation secondary to persistent epithelial defects, 34 eyes (61.8%) achieved a postoperative visual acuity of 0.6 logMAR or better, and three-year graft survival was 65.1% and 63.6% in the two groups. The opacity is thus documented both as measured optical degradation and as the operative indication.

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) severity and organism dependence - the located eyes come from referral and surgical populations selected for scarring, so no cohort quantifies the proportion of keratitis episodes that leave a permanent opacity and mild epithelial disease resolves without residual scarring; (ii) pathway specificity - the adenoviral subepithelial-infiltrate route belongs to the conjunctivitis window and is not restated, while the located keratitis evidence is bacterial, fungal, Acanthamoeba, and herpes simplex stromal disease; (iii) structural rather than functional framing - the Shimizu cohort quantifies opacity grading and higher-order aberrations, so the edge records a structural and optical sequela and deliberately does not make the closed visual-impairment claim; (iv) treatment modification - the keratoplasty series measures outcomes after surgery, so the scarring is characterised as an indication rather than as an unmodified natural-history end point.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no keratitis-to-visual-impairment edge - the harvested proposition remains FINAL-CLOSED under FINAL-CLOSE-PROPOSITION-MISMATCH and is not reasserted (prior-closure guard); (ii) no blindness or night-blindness edge - no condition-specific keratitis cohort quantifying legal blindness or nyctalopia was retrieved in this batch window (zero-record guard); (iii) no keratitis-to-glaucoma, cataracts, uveitis, or corneal-ulceration edge - no condition-specific quantification was retrieved and those identities carry windows from their own primaries (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (iv) no keratitis-to-dry-eye-syndrome edge - the existing dry-eye window is authored from its own primaries and keratitis is often the consequence rather than the cause of ocular-surface disease (duplicate-scope and direction guards); (v) duplicate-scope note recorded in todo: the corneal-scarring identity's adenoviral and cicatricial windows are not pre-empted and this batch adds a distinct microbial and herpetic stromal window.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Shimizu 2017 retrospective consecutive series examined 63 eyes of 62 patients with corneal scarring due to Acanthamoeba keratitis (20 eyes), bacterial keratitis (35 eyes), and fungal keratitis (8 eyes) together with 18 normal subjects, finding total-cornea higher-order aberrations within a 4-mm diameter significantly larger in the keratitis eyes (Acanthamoeba 1.15 +/- 2.06 micrometre, bacterial 0.91 +/- 0.88, fungal 1.39 +/- 1.46) than in controls (0.09 +/- 0.01, all P < .001), an asymmetric topographic pattern as the commonest (30%, 51.4%, and 37.5%), and visual acuity correlating significantly with anterior-surface (R = 0.764), posterior-surface (R = 0.745), and total-cornea (R = 0.669) aberrations (all P < .0001); the Altay 2017 retrospective analysis of 55 eyes undergoing penetrating keratoplasty for corneal scarring caused by herpes simplex keratitis reported 42 eyes with a quiescent herpetic scar and 13 with a descemetocele or perforation secondary to persistent epithelial defects, with 34 eyes (61.8%) reaching 0.6 logMAR or better and three-year graft survival of 65.1% and 63.6%; the literature documents corneal opacity as the structural sequela that degrades ocular-surface optics and that serves as the operative indication, without establishing that any individual's scarring followed the keratitis episode.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: no cohort quantifies the incidence of permanent corneal opacity after a defined keratitis episode, mild epithelial disease resolves without residual scarring, the located series are tertiary referral and surgical populations selected for severity, the degree of opacity depends on organism, depth of stromal involvement, treatment delay, and host response, and unrelated corneal disease (trauma, contact-lens pathology, ectasia, degenerations, dystrophies, and surgical scarring) produces identical opacification - so no directional claim is made at the keratitis level.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: An infectious-keratitis-to-stromal-opacity route is documented: microbial or herpetic invasion of the corneal epithelium and stroma provokes a neutrophilic and immune-mediated infiltrate with stromal oedema and necrosis, and as the infiltrate resolves collagen remodelling and myofibroblast repair deposit irregular matrix - producing subepithelial and stromal opacity that scatters light and flattens the refractive surface, documented as graded corneal opacity and increased higher-order aberrations whose magnitude correlates with visual acuity and, in the most severe pattern, as scarring with descemetocele or perforation requiring penetrating keratoplasty; the pathway is organism- and depth-dependent, so the individual course remains a hypothesis.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Corneal opacity is the documented structural sequela of infectious keratitis in graded-opacity, higher-order-aberration, and keratoplasty cohorts, but individual determination requires documentation of the keratitis episode with aetiology and dates, slit-lamp and topographic documentation of the opacity localizing it to the cornea, exclusion of independent corneal disease, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Ophthalmologic documentation of the keratitis episode(s) with aetiology where available (bacterial, fungal, Acanthamoeba, herpetic, or other), laterality, severity, depth of stromal involvement, and treatment with dates; slit-lamp and anterior-segment imaging or corneal topography documenting the opacity, its location and depth, and the presence or absence of vascularization or thinning; refraction, visual acuity, and any higher-order-aberration measurement with chronology relative to the keratitis; documentation of prior contact-lens wear, ocular trauma, ocular surgery, dry-eye disease, and any coexisting corneal dystrophy, degeneration, or ectasia; exclusion of independent causes of corneal opacity (traumatic or surgical scarring, keratoconus or other ectasia, Salzmann nodular degeneration, corneal dystrophies, and cicatricial conjunctival disease); ophthalmologic assessment of whether the keratitis episode materially contributed to the documented opacity
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Traumatic or surgical corneal scarring unrelated to the keratitis episode
Contact-lens-related hypoxia or solution toxicity keratopathy without infection
Corneal dystrophies (for example granular, lattice, or macular dystrophy) and degenerations
Cicatricial conjunctival disease (for example ocular cicatricial pemphigoid or Stevens-Johnson sequelae)

evidenceGaps: Ophthalmologic documentation of the keratitis episode(s) with aetiology where available (bacterial, fungal, Acanthamoeba, herpetic, or other), laterality, severity, depth of stromal involvement, and treatment with dates; slit-lamp and anterior-segment imaging or corneal topography documenting the opacity, its location and depth, and the presence or absence of vascularization or thinning; refraction, visual acuity, and any higher-order-aberration measurement with chronology relative to the keratitis; documentation of prior contact-lens wear, ocular trauma, ocular surgery, dry-eye disease, and any coexisting corneal dystrophy, degeneration, or ectasia; exclusion of independent causes of corneal opacity (traumatic or surgical scarring, keratoconus or other ectasia, Salzmann nodular degeneration, corneal dystrophies, and cicatricial conjunctival disease); ophthalmologic assessment of whether the keratitis episode materially contributed to the documented opacity
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a 63-eye consecutive series with corneal scarring due to bacterial, fungal, and Acanthamoeba keratitis measured opacity grading and higher-order aberrations significantly above normal controls with visual acuity correlating with the aberrations, and a 55-eye keratoplasty series documents herpes simplex keratitis scarring as the surgical indication with a descemetocele or perforation in 13 eyes. The evidence is referral- and surgery-selected and quantifies optical and structural sequelae rather than the probability that a given keratitis episode leaves a permanent opacity, so the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and deliberately avoids the FINAL-CLOSED visual-impairment proposition; individual claims require the keratitis characterization, opacity documentation, chronology, and competing-cause exclusion recorded in the evidence gaps.
